claims.claim: the merge subject `fleet land` PRINTS is the one it tells the supervisor to RUN: `next: git merge --no-ff -m 'merge(w1/example): <summary>' w1/example`. Before this lane it printed the short lane (`merge(w1)`) beside a command merging `w1/example`, and `wave-close` resolves that subject token as a BRANCH, so every lane merged the documented way joined to nothing (queue item 26-i).

the worker record keeps the BRANCH it was dispatched on: `new_worker_record(..., branch=...)` writes it beside `cwd`, `cmd_spawn` and `_cmd_respawn_native` fill it from `_worktree_branch(cwd)` (which reads the worktree's own `.git`/HEAD file -- stdlib, no subprocess on the dispatch path), and `tests/test_core.py`'s schema test pins the field. That branch is the join key the routine `git worktree remove` does NOT delete (queue item 16).

`_wave_lane_join` resolves a merge-subject lane to its registry record by BRANCH first and by worktree `cwd` second, so a lane stays attributable after its worktree is pruned: `_wave_merge_audit`, `_wave_record_substrate`, `_wave_codex_tokens`, `_wave_outcomes_claude_tokens`, `_wave_external_lines` and `_wave_mark_landed_lanes` all read through it. Item 19's stop-then-reap arm marks the lane landed by the branch join with the worktree gone.

a lane that PARSES but joins to no registry record and no worktree REFUSES the close -- `wave-close: UNJOINED: N of M landed lane(s) in <base>..HEAD resolve to no registry record and no worktree (...)`, beside item 14's `UNPARSED` refusal and before the claim, the reap and the floor, so an unjoinable lane can no longer be published as `unknown`/`0`/`UNMEASURED`. Wave 86's `workers: 2 (w93: unknown, w92: unknown); tokens: 0; tokens_per_bin_line: 0.00; ... reaped: 0` on a 701-line wave is unreachable three ways now.

an unreadable substrate is no longer a confident zero: a lane whose substrate reads `unknown` makes `tokens` and `tokens_per_bin_line` UNMEASURED rather than `0`, and `_wave_outcomes_claude_tokens` returns UNMEASURED (lane substrate unknown) instead of summing the remaining lanes and printing the shortfall as measured (queue item 26-a).

RED-FIRST, measured not asserted: the 9 new/changed tests were re-run against a `git archive HEAD` copy of the pre-change tree with the new test files copied in, and 10 failed there -- 8 for the missing join or the missing refusal (`AttributeError: module 'fleet' has no attribute '_wave_lane_join'`, `assert [] == ['w99']`, the UNJOINED regex matching nothing, `TypeError: new_worker_record() got an unexpected keyword argument 'branch'`) and 2 on real assertions (`unknown` versus the recorded substrate, and the printed short-lane merge subject).
